days.label: Monday, October 19
days.note: Automated edition. Sunday night's seed list is folded up below. No race review today: Austin is next weekend.

items.t: Ornot's waterproof, packable new cycling jacket thought of everything
items.d: A real hands-on test, ridden in the rain from Manhattan to Queens. The stuff-sack pocket and two-way zipper are the details that win it over.

items.t: Leisure Travel Vans Wonder FX motorhome
items.d: A sub-25-foot Transit-based camper with a Murphy bed and optional AWD. One-minute daydream material.

items.t: Triplet of 'ghostly' galaxies hints at what dark matter is, and isn't
items.d: Three faint galaxies seem to have almost no dark matter, and the best explanation is an ancient collision that stripped it away. A cosmic whodunit, about 7 minutes.

items.t: Here's how freaky the universe would look if light slowed to 3 miles per hour
items.d: A short piece about a browser toy that lets you walk around a world where light moves at walking pace. Three minutes to read, then something to click on.

items.t: Portrait of a Scaphander
items.d: From the Belgica's brutal Antarctic winter of 1898 to the first underwater photographs and blind cave creatures, following the naturalist Emil Racovita. About 3,800 words.

items.t: 11 retirement planning mistakes that haunt high-earning physicians
items.d: Mid-career traps: too much pre-tax money that becomes an RMD and IRMAA problem, SEP IRA instead of a Solo 401(k) or cash balance plan, and deadlines that fall well before December.

items.t: Who got richer since 2022?
items.d: New Fed data: households over 75 gained about 38 percent while the under-35s lost ground. Maggiulli's takeaway is to give to your kids earlier. 9 minutes.

items.t: What one image can't show you about the Rwanda F1 track
items.d: Alex Wurz walks through the elevation and braking zones of the new Kigali circuit that a single render cannot convey. 6 minutes.

items.t: Toto Wolff issues reality check as Kimi Antonelli closes in on the title
items.d: Antonelli is 102 points clear and can clinch in Austin with a win and the right gap to Russell and Hamilton. Wolff doubts it happens this weekend.

items.t: Planet Money: Anatomy of a movie market
items.d: 32 minutes. Riding along with the 'King of Sundance' as he sells a slate of indie films to Netflix, Sony and Apple, with the backstories of Little Miss Sunshine and Napoleon Dynamite.

items.t: Unexplainable: What's cooler than being cool?
items.d: 29 minutes. Why quantum computers have to be chilled to near the coldest temperatures in the universe, and the race to build the refrigerators that get them there.

items.t: Today, Explained: The cost of loving your pet
items.d: 30 minutes. How our bonds with pets deepened after the pandemic, and how the bills climbed with them.

items.t: I electrified my push scooter with a power drill
items.d: A cordless drill bolted to the front wheel of a Razor scooter, with one-way bearings so it still coasts. About 10 mph and 2 miles of range. Did not save money, was worth it anyway.

items.t: World first: a southern ground hornbill gets 3D printed beak prostheses at Artis Zoo
items.d: Amsterdam's zoo and Utrecht's vets rebuilt a broken beak in two printed pieces. The bird started using it the same day.

items.t: There's never been a better time to go into math
items.d: Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown on why AI proving theorems makes math more inviting, not less. A 35 minute video, so save it for a lunch break.

items.t: Why some people mow a lawn better than others
items.d: Mow a virtual lawn as efficiently as you can, then see how your route compares with 132,000 other people and the mathematically optimal path. Oddly competitive.

days.label: Monday, October 19
days.note: First edition. Seeded Sunday night; the automated version starts tomorrow.

items.t: Yeti's first technical jacket should put Patagonia and The North Face on notice
items.d: The cooler company made a shell. Gear Patrol thinks it is a real contender.

items.t: Ressence Type 10 DN
items.d: A watch with no hands: oil-filled discs rotate inside each other. 100 made.

items.t: Sea monkeys show scientists how to rewrite a rule of turbulence
items.d: Brine shrimp swimming in a tank reversed the direction energy is supposed to flow in turbulent water.

items.t: Life after death?
items.d: Thousands of people answered what they think comes next. A scrolling visual essay, about 8 minutes.

items.t: Jos Verstappen was hyped like Max, until it all went wrong
items.d: The father's career, which explains a lot about the son.

items.t: Invest vs. pay off debt: what should you do with extra cash?
items.d: Listener questions on debt payoff versus investing, practice buy-ins, and account types.

items.t: 'My spirit animal is now the sloth': how real retirees withdraw money
items.d: Survey answers from retired physicians on how they actually spend down.

items.t: How Horner, Brown and Wolff made their fortunes from F1
items.d: UK company accounts, so the numbers are real. Horner's exit payment is the headline.

items.t: What Ferrari is changing with its biggest upgrade of 2026
items.d: New floor for Austin this weekend, the last big push before the 2027 car.

items.t: Chequered Flag Extra: F1 super subs and the home Grand Prix curse
items.d: Latest episode, 30 minutes. Streams free on BBC Sounds without an account.

items.t: 99% Invisible: (Not Just) Another Brick in the Wall
items.d: 28 minutes on Chicago's strange handmade bricks and why they look the way they do.

items.t: Today, Explained: Data centers fight back
items.d: 26 minutes. The PR war to make AI infrastructure likable.

items.t: Sigsaly: Churchill's top secret hotline to the President
items.d: The encrypted phone in the Cabinet War Rooms, and how it worked.

items.t: The Zelda timeline, to catch up before the Ocarina of Time remake
items.d: A fan-built interactive timeline of every game. Pure nostalgia.

items.t: Going 94 mph on a skateboard, new world record
items.d: Diego Poncelet, 151.8 km/h, downhill. Watch the video before coffee.

items.t: The online Library of Babel
items.d: Every possible page of text already exists here. Search for a sentence you just wrote and it will find it.
